approach: Add one shared private const CHECKABLE_CRITERIA_RULE to briefs.rs. Render it in the reader brief as its own `# Checkable criteria` section (after the code survey guide, before `# What the verifier can run`), so READING_RULES and its tests are untouched. Render it in the producer brief as a new `## Make your evidence checkable` section (fn checkable_evidence_section) just before criteria_check_section. The producer section says: prefer a test in your change; add a file only when a deliverable or criterion names it; the report is still where you state what you ran or read; a criterion provable only from the report is reported unmet, with evidence that begins with the fixed phrase `not checkable by the verifier`. Two tests render the briefs and assert on their text. In structure-pass.md section 5, each report-held proof becomes something in the snapshot (the committed tests and code the verifier builds and runs) or a command the verifier reruns (the old-path Grep, `--list`, `git diff`). Item 3 keeps its named exceptions (mod/use/visibility lines, the R5-R8 Flow::Stop and seam-struct lines, the G1 guard constant and D87/D88 paths) and only moves the check from the report to the diff. Item 5 says the proof is in the snapshot: committed tests compile and run every hit, the 5.1 test covers the PrHost fakes, and a diff showing no old-path line added or removed outside moved blocks makes the before and after counts equal by construction, so no count is stored. No new evidence file or docs note, so items 1, 4 and 7 stay true. One CHANGELOG line. No refusal logic, prompt file or governance file changes.

decisions.reason: READING_RULES is [&str; 8] and tests (~4476-4521) assert len 8, one check named per line, lines <=220 bytes and the section <2600 bytes. The rule adds no check (check_criteria_evidence stays as is). Its own `# ` heading ends the rules section at the next `\n# `, so those tests read the same text.

decisions.choice: Producer section text: the shared rule; 'Prefer a test in your change that shows the property. Add a new file for evidence only when a deliverable or a criterion names it. Your report is still where you state what you ran or read; the rule only means the verifier does not rely on it. If a criterion can be shown only from your report, report it unmet and begin its evidence with `not checkable by the verifier`; do not invent a file.' (answers finding 2)
decisions.reason: criteria_check_section (briefs.rs 746-760) requires every non-left-to-Athena criterion to be reported met with evidence, so the uncheckable case needs a status. Unmet is honest. Cost, stated plainly: unmet_criteria (run/send_back.rs:18) counts any non-Met entry, so producer.rs sends the work back once (PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1, run/mod.rs:1549); the producer cannot fix the criterion wording, so that send-back is one wasted run; after it the gap reaches the verifier through report_gaps (run/producer.rs:528, run/verification.rs:100-108). The fixed opening phrase lets the verifier and a maintainer read the gap in report_gaps as 'cannot be checked' and not as missing work. The extra sentence keeps true that the report still states what was run or read.

decisions.choice: Item 5 wording (answers findings 3 and 4): 'Caller check. The proof is in the snapshot, not in the report. Every hit of each moved name's old path (for example gh::GhClient, gh::land_pr, run::send_back_text) over crates/ is compiled and run by the committed tests (cargo test --locked), and the fake hosts implementing PrHost are covered by the test named in 5.1. The verifier reruns the Grep for each old path over crates/ on the candidate and reads git diff -U0 -- crates/, which must show no line holding an old path removed or added outside moved blocks; that makes the before and after counts equal by construction, so no count is stored in a report.'
decisions.reason: Criterion 3 asks that the caller-check evidence be in the snapshot (a committed file or test). The committed tests and code are the snapshot evidence and the rerun makes it checkable. The 'a stored before count cannot be rechecked' sentence is dropped (the base commit is in the candidate repository, so a before count could be recomputed); the real argument is that the diff check already proves the counts equal. A new file or note is blocked by items 4 and 7, and new test lines by item 1, so existing committed tests are the only snapshot evidence that does not break another item. The conflict between 'file or test' and items 1/4/7 stays an open question for the user. The step-9 report quotes this item 5 sentence so a verifier can map it to criterion 3.

decisions.choice: Item 3 keeps its exceptions and moves the check from the report to the diff (answers finding 1). Text: '`git diff -M --color-moved=zebra` (or `--color-moved-ws=ignore-all-space` for re-indented bodies) shows the moved blocks as moved. The verifier reads the diff: every line not marked moved is a `mod`, `use`, `pub use` or visibility line, or one of the edits this section names: the `Flow::Stop` and seam-struct lines of the R5-R8 bullets below, and, in G1, the guard constant and the D87/D88 `paths` of 5.2. Any other unmoved line fails the job.'
decisions.reason: Original lines 226-228 say 'the only expected ones are mod, use, pub use and visibility lines' while lines 249-253 (R5-R8 Flow::Stop and struct fields), 261-265 (D87/D88 paths) and 268-275 (WRAPPER constant) require other unmoved lines. A bare 'must be mod/use/visibility' would fail those jobs and change the moves. Naming the exceptions keeps the rule consistent with item 1, which already allows the G1 guard constant.

risks.risk: An uncheckable criterion reported 'unmet' costs one wasted producer send-back: unmet_criteria counts any non-Met entry, producer.rs sends back once, and the producer cannot fix wording that belongs to the reading. After that the gap reaches the verifier through report_gaps.
risks.mitigation: Accepted cost, since a met claim on an uncheckable criterion is worse. The fixed phrase `not checkable by the verifier` marks the gap in report_gaps; the reader-side rule is meant to stop such criteria before a producer sees them, so the case should be rare. No send-back logic changes.

risks.mitigation: Criterion 6's `git diff --stat` and `git status`, and step 9, catch it; the plan places all text in Rust-built briefs and adds no evidence file.

risks.mitigation: Out of scope; the rewrite touches only evidence sentences. The 5.2 sentence names the existing test, which passes against the current paths.
